newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Court jails Mozambique policemen for beating death.
newsitem.headline: Court jails Mozambique policemen for beating death.

text.p: A Maputo court on Thursday jailed four policemen for seven years for beating a suspect to death in an attempt to force a confession.
Under Mozambican law the crime of involuntary homicide, with which the men were charged, carries a prison term of between two and eight years.

Judge Rafael Sebastiao ruled the policemen had tried to beat a confession out of Frenque Tchembene but had not intended to kill him. Tchembene was arrested last June for the theft of a truck he had earlier reported stolen.

The court found officer Abilio Lisboa had ordered two of his juniors, Constantino Namicopo and Joao Palane, to beat a confession out of Tchembene. The court also jailed police commander Marciano Chihale for not trying to stop it.
Tchembene died in Maputo's central hospital after the intervention of the Mozambican Human Rights League.
